parts: The first product ever scanned with today's barcode was a pack of chewing gum.
Norman Joseph Woodland went to Miami Beach to think. Inspired by Morse code, he drew long and short lines in the sand with his fingers.
Then he swept them around into a circle, like a target.
The code we use today is a rectangle, designed by an IBM engineer named George Laurer.
On June twenty-sixth, nineteen seventy-four, in Troy, Ohio, cashier Sharon Buchanan scanned a pack of Juicy Fruit gum.
Legend says it was chosen on purpose.
